newsitem.title: USA: Actress Marjorie Reynolds dies aged 77.
newsitem.headline: Actress Marjorie Reynolds dies aged 77.

text.p: Actress Marjorie Reynolds, who sang and danced her way into Americans' hearts in the 1940s as the love interest of Bing Crosby and Fred Astaire in the movie "Holiday Inn" has died, a family spokesman said on Thursday.

Reynolds, who also endeared herself to television audiences as Peg Riley in the 1950s TV series, "The Life of Riley," died at home in the Los Angeles suburb of Manhattan Beach of congestive heart failure on Feb. 1, the spokesman, a member of the family, said. She was 77.
The actress was born in Idaho and moved with her family to Los Angeles where she began acting as a child under the stage name Marjorie Moore. She was born Marjorie Goodspeed.
She changed her name to Marjorie Reynolds when she married screenwriter Jack Reynolds. They later divorced and she married film editor Jon Haffen, who died in 1985.

Reynolds made over 50 films, many of which were B movies and westerns, but she is best remembered as the willowy blonde courted by Bing Crosby and Fred Astaire in the 1942 Irving Berlin classic which is re-run on television each Christmas holiday season, featuring Crosby singing "White Christmas."

The film marked Reynolds' peak of fame in the movie industry and although she went on to make other films such as "Bring on the Girls" in 1945 and "Meet Me on Broadway" a year later, her movie career sputtered.
Then, in 1953, she found fame again in the new media of television as the ever-optimistic wife of William Bendix in "The Life of Riley."
The series lasted from 1953 to 1957, and when it ended Reynolds career effectively ended with it.
She is survived by a daughter who lives in Los Angeles.
